Tegata Checkout is a pay button for any website. Your page loads one script from tegata.xyz; a button opens
Tegata's pay page over your page; the customer pays; your server hears about it from a signed webhook. The business
always receives exactly the price, in USDC on NEAR.

<Callout title="Try it" type="info">
The [demo shop](https://docs.tegata.xyz/demo-shop) on this docs site (a different origin from tegata.xyz) has three real buttons on
Sandbox pay links. Paying them takes test dollars, not real money.
</Callout>

## Quickstart

<Steps>
<Step>
### Load the script, once per page

```html
<script src="https://tegata.xyz/checkout.js" defer></script>
```
</Step>
<Step>
### Put a button where you want it

```html
<button data-tegata-link="TOKEN"></button>
```

`TOKEN` is your pay link's token, the last part of its address: `https://tegata.xyz/pay/3h7CkB7muWUM` has the token
`3h7CkB7muWUM`. Make a link under [Pay links](/docs/guide/pay-links), or let **Checkout** build the code for you.
</Step>
</Steps>

That's all. An empty element gets Tegata's own button; press it and the checkout opens over your page.

## The Checkout page in the app

<Shot src="/shots/wide/app-checkout.webp" alt="The Checkout page in Tegata: What it charges, a list of Studio Kaze's pay links (Tip the studio, any amount, chosen; Seal print, A5, $2.50; Washi tote bag, $1.00; Design sprint, Week 2, $0.25); Amount on the button 42.50; Look: Vermilion, Ink, Washi and Small, Medium, Large; Show the coins; beside them a shop page at your-shop.com with the button and What your customer sees; below, the code in tabs index.html, PayButton.tsx and no-script.html, with Copy" caption="Real: Get paid → Checkout builds the button and its code." address="tegata.xyz/app/checkout" />

Open **Checkout** under **Get paid** in the rail. Choose **What it charges** (one of your open pay links; the page
lists six), the **Amount
on the button** for an any-amount link, the **Look** (Vermilion, Ink or Washi; Small, Medium or Large) and **Show the
coins**. A shop page shows the real button; press it for the real checkout. The code comes in three tabs,
`index.html`, `PayButton.tsx` and `no-script.html`, each with **Copy**.

## The attributes

checkout.js wires every element with `data-tegata-link` or `data-tegata-session`, including ones added to the page
later.

| Attribute | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `data-tegata-link` | A pay link's token. The checkout charges that link |
| `data-tegata-session` | A [checkout session](/docs/build/developers#checkout-sessions)'s pay URL (its `url`) or token. Use it when your server sets the price per order |
| `data-tegata-amount` | Dollars, like `42.50`. Drawn on the button; for an any-amount link it is also the amount the checkout starts with (the payer can change it). On a fixed-price link it is only drawn, so keep it equal to the link's price |
| `data-tegata-theme` | `shu` (vermilion, the default), `ink` or `washi`. `dark` means `ink`, `light` means `washi` |
| `data-tegata-size` | `s`, `m` or `l`: 40, 48 or 56 pixels tall. `m` by default |
| `data-tegata-coins` | `off` hides the coin marks on the button |

An element with its own content keeps your markup: put text or an image inside and checkout.js only wires the click
(and, on an element that isn't a `<button>`, adds `role="button"` and a tab stop). An empty element gets Tegata's
button, drawn in a Shadow DOM so your page's CSS can't change it.

## From JavaScript

```js
Tegata.checkout({
  link: "3h7CkB7muWUM",        // or session: "https://tegata.xyz/pay/zFydXvEnyZjFzF"
  amount: "12.50",             // any-amount links: where it starts
  onPaid: (detail) => {},      // { paymentId, amount, receipt }
  onClose: ({ reason }) => {}, // "closed", "backdrop", "escape" or "replaced"
  target: document.querySelector("#buy"), // gets the DOM events below
})

Tegata.close()
```

| Option | |
| --- | --- |
| `link` or `session` | One of them. A session can be its pay URL or its token |
| `amount` | Dollars, for an any-amount link |
| `onPaid(detail)` | When the payment has settled. `detail` is `{ paymentId, amount, receipt }`: `amount` in USDC base units as a string (`"1000000"` is $1.00), `receipt` the receipt's address, or `null` |
| `onClose({ reason })` | When the checkout closes: its close button, a click outside it, Escape (while your page has focus), or another checkout opening |
| `target` | An element that receives `tegata:paid` and `tegata:closed` |

<Shot src="/shots/wide/shop-tip.webp" alt="The demo shop with the checkout open from the shop's own Send a tip button: Pay Studio Kaze, Tip the studio, $12.50, the amount the shop typed, still editable; How do you want to pay? Tegata balance, NEAR wallet, Another chain" caption="Real: the shop's own button and Tegata.checkout, opening an any-amount link at $12.50." address="docs.tegata.xyz/demo-shop" />

Buttons wired from attributes are their own target. Both events bubble, so one listener on `document` hears every
button:

```js
document.addEventListener("tegata:paid", (event) => {
  console.log(event.detail) // { paymentId, amount, receipt }
})
document.addEventListener("tegata:closed", () => {})
```

On a screen 520 pixels wide or less, the checkout rises from the bottom; on a wider one it sits in the middle. Loading
the script twice does no harm.

## React and Next.js

Load the script once, and render plain buttons. checkout.js finds them when they appear.

```tsx title="PayButton.tsx"
"use client"
import { useEffect } from "react"

const SRC = "https://tegata.xyz/checkout.js"

export function PayButton({ link, amount }: { link: string; amount?: string }) {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (document.querySelector(`script[src="${SRC}"]`)) return
    const script = document.createElement("script")
    script.src = SRC
    script.defer = true
    document.body.appendChild(script)
  }, [])

  // A new key when the amount changes, so the button is drawn again with it.
  return <button key={amount} data-tegata-link={link} data-tegata-amount={amount} />
}
```

In the Next.js App Router, load it from the root layout with `next/script` and open the checkout from a client
component. Here the price comes from your server, as a [checkout session](/docs/build/developers#checkout-sessions):

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import Script from "next/script"

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        {children}
        <Script src="https://tegata.xyz/checkout.js" strategy="afterInteractive" />
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

```tsx title="app/cart/pay.tsx"
"use client"
import { useRouter } from "next/navigation"

declare global {
  interface Window {
    Tegata?: {
      checkout(options: {
        link?: string
        session?: string
        amount?: string
        onPaid?: (detail: { paymentId: string; amount: string; receipt: string | null }) => void
        onClose?: (info: { reason: string }) => void
        target?: Element
      }): void
      close(): void
    }
  }
}

export function Pay({ sessionUrl }: { sessionUrl: string }) {
  const router = useRouter()
  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      onClick={() =>
        window.Tegata?.checkout({
          session: sessionUrl,
          // For the screen only: the order is confirmed by your webhook handler.
          onPaid: () => router.push("/thanks"),
        })
      }
    >
      Pay with Tegata
    </button>
  )
}
```

`sessionUrl` is the `url` your server got back when it created the session with its secret API key. Never put the
key in the browser.

## No JavaScript

The same button as an image, linking to the pay page:

```html
<a href="https://tegata.xyz/pay/TOKEN">
  <img src="https://tegata.xyz/checkout/button.svg?amount=42.50&theme=shu"
       alt="Pay $42.50 with Tegata" height="48">
</a>
```

| `button.svg` parameter | |
| --- | --- |
| `amount` | Dollars, like `42.50` (up to nine digits and two decimals). Left out, the button reads "Tegata" |
| `theme` | `shu`, `ink` or `washi`. Anything else draws `shu` |
| `size` | `s`, `m` or `l` (40, 48 or 56 pixels tall). Anything else draws `m` |
| `coins` | `0` hides the coins |

The image is one SVG with the words drawn as outlines, so it looks the same on every site without a font, and it is
cached for a day. For an any-amount link, add `?amount=12.50` to the pay page's address and the page starts there.

## How the customer pays

The checkout is Tegata's [pay page](/docs/guide/pay-page), the same one `https://tegata.xyz/pay/TOKEN` opens:

| Way | |
| --- | --- |
| **Tegata balance** | Sign in with an email and pay from Tegata dollars. In the Sandbox, **Add $5.00 test dollars** appears when the balance is short. Signing in takes the payer to Tegata's sign-in page and back to the plain pay page, so the payment works but your page doesn't hear `onPaid` from it: your webhook still arrives |
| **NEAR wallet** | Approve one USDC transfer with the payment's memo |
| **Another chain** (Live) | USDT, USDC, BTC, ETH or SOL: 20 coin-and-chain routes on 11 chains, through NEAR Intents, picked coin first, then chain. The payer gives a refund address on their chain, then sends exactly the quoted amount to a deposit address before the "Pay within" time runs out: from a wallet on the device (EVM wallets found through EIP-6963, such as MetaMask, Rabby, Coinbase Wallet and OKX, or TronLink: "Connect, then approve one transfer", which also fills the refund address), or from any wallet or exchange to the address or QR code |
| **Card** | Through Transak, once its keys are set ([Cards](/docs/guide/cards#customers-who-pay-by-card)) |

Payers on another chain start on USDC on Base. A route below its minimum says so in dollars ("USDC on Base needs at
least $0.15 right now", "USDT on Tron needs at least $100 right now"), with a one-tap switch to Base. In the Sandbox, another chain shows the real price and pays in Live only.

The bar on top of the checkout has **Open in a new window**, for a sign-in or a wallet that won't work inside another
site's frame. It opens the same pay page in a tab of its own (without an amount you preset). Your page hears nothing
from that tab; the webhook arrives as always.

## Security

- **The browser event is not proof.** `onPaid`, `tegata:paid` and the messages behind them are for your screens.
  Confirm an order from the signed [webhook](/docs/build/developers#webhooks), or by reading the session with your
  API key.
- **An any-amount link takes what the payer sends.** The amount you set is where the page starts, and the payer can
  change it. Check the webhook's `amount` against the order, or use a checkout session: its price is set by your
  server and can't be changed.
- **A pay link has no order number.** Its `payment.succeeded` names the link (`request_id`) and the amount. For
  orders, make a session per order and put the order in its `metadata`.
- **Only the checkout can be framed.** Other sites may load `https://tegata.xyz/checkout/<token>` in a frame; every
  other Tegata page refuses to load in another site's frame (`frame-ancestors 'self'`), so nobody can frame the app
  where an owner approves money.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="The messages between the checkout and your page">

checkout.js opens `https://tegata.xyz/checkout/<token>?parent=<your page's origin>` in an iframe. The checkout sends
messages only to that origin, with `postMessage`:

| `type` | When | Carries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tegata:checkout.opened` | The checkout loaded | `token` |
| `tegata:checkout.completed` | The payment settled | `token`, `detail: { paymentId, amount, receipt }` |
| `tegata:checkout.close` | The payer pressed close | `token` |

checkout.js acts on a message only if it comes from tegata.xyz, from its own frame, for the token it opened.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Sandbox and Live

A pay link or session belongs to the mode it was made in. A Sandbox link charges test dollars on NEAR testnet; a Live
one charges real USDC on NEAR mainnet, and only there can a customer pay from another chain (NEAR Intents has no
testnet). The script, the attributes and the events are the same in both.
